note: How the Storm Crossing Crew's return forecast (data/world/return_crossing.json) is laid on the level's real return route. scripts/world/crossing_sequence.gd reads this file. The forecast's 600 m route is stretched along the straight line from the Saltgate quay to the harbour mouth; its lanes are lateral offsets from that line (left and right as seen heading home). One forecast drives the hazards, the safe-lane signal and Arthur's calls, so they can never disagree.
spawn_note: The hazards are placed when the level is ready (creator, 31 Oct 2026), so the sea is the same on the outbound and the return crossings: the outbound has to weave round them too.

near_miss.note: A near miss (outbound or return) is a pass within edge_m (2.5 m, closer than first tried: the creator liked it nearer the rocks) of a sea stack or a hazard without touching it. Each leg counts them, and Arthur's line gets more frantic each time (ARTHUR_NEAR_1, _2, _3; the third repeats).

calls.note: Arthur's calls are dialogue lines whose trigger is the call id (ARTHUR_RET_01 ...), played when the boat's route position passes the call's trigger_route_m.

end_note: The forecast's 600 m ends here, 35 m south of the island's rim at the harbour mouth, so no hazard lands on the island or in the harbour; the boat's own docking takes it the rest of the way (RETURN_ARRIVED).

return_collision.note: A collision on the return (creator, 31 Oct 2026): the boat is thrown back 3 m from what it hit over 0.9 s (11 m was too far) and rocks very hard for about 2.5 s (38 degrees of roll at the start), instead of being put back at the last clear spot, and the deadline is charged 5 s. Outbound collisions keep the old recovery and cost nothing.

docking.note: DOCKING_DIALOGUE plays every time auto-docking starts. At the lighthouse after a return with collisions it is replaced by an admonishment: tier 1 for 1 hit, 2 for 2-3, 3 for 4 or more (DOCKING_DIALOGUE_LIGHTHOUSE_1..3).
